title: Aravil

body:
Aravil arrives hungry, lonely, and still defined by service. She describes herself as a tool separated from its artisan, but corrects Magnus when he assumes that means she wants a new master: her oath remains while she draws breath. Separation has taken away proximity, not obligation.

Her wider history gives that discipline a social dimension. Aravil remembers adventurers by the work they did under pressure, and they remember her in return. She does not need to perform experience because shared history has already made it visible.

Action after judgment

Aravil is direct and decisive. Once she believes a fight has truly arrived, she commits without demanding a speech first. In October 2025, when the company presses toward a demonic island, she heads into the battle rather than waiting for ceremony. In a crisis she draws on her training and judges where to fight. The account does not portray that readiness as indiscriminate bloodlust.

The people she remembers

When Aravil meets Jiangshi again, she recalls their Fey Forest hunt with Scribonia and even Jiangshi’s “violent hairpins.” The specificity is the point. Affection and respect appear as operational memory: a hunt, a method, a moment of competence. Olokun likewise greets her as a returning veteran rather than a new arrival, and Aravil answers the thrum of war as though returning to unfinished work.

Admitting error

She openly says she involved herself in a conflict without knowing the people or their capabilities. Competence does not require pretending she was right. The admission becomes part of her posture toward a world she is still learning.

Useful belonging

Later, Pristinia’s food shortage gives Aravil a local role. She recognizes that her hunting skills can help feed the town while she remains sworn to her Queen.

Watching institutions reveal themselves

During the December 2025 conflict surrounding Elenia, Magnus, Olokun, and Zarathian religious authority, Aravil watches to see whether demonstrated power will actually make the society reconsider its traditions. Her attention is not passive curiosity. She tests the institution by its response: will it bend, learn, and admit contradiction, or merely invent a new rule that protects the old hierarchy?

This skepticism belongs beside her martial directness. Aravil prefers enemies, customs, and authorities to reveal what they truly are. Once they do, she can judge them by their conduct rather than their claims.

A veteran carried by mutual memory

Aravil’s history accumulates through recognition rather than constant spotlight. Jiangshi’s hairpins, Scribonia’s presence on the Fey Forest hunt, and Olokun’s familiar greeting preserve a network of old operational bonds. She remembers companions through what they did under pressure, and their recognition confirms that her own earlier deeds remain part of the living world.

Her development is therefore continuity across absence: skilled participant, remembered veteran, and finally a piece of shared history who can return without being reintroduced. Aravil makes the archive’s persistence visible. People who leave the foreground do not cease to matter when the world continues to remember them.

Getting Icarus past the patrol

When the Gate activates amid the Rahu threat, Aravil runs to reach the newcomer first. She warns Icarus to hide, remains concealed while he becomes a chicken, and waits out the search. Once the patrol leaves, she begins answering his questions and leads him toward Pristinia. Her preference for striking back does not prevent her from accepting a successful escape without combat. Read Icarus’s account.

Babel · skill, supplies and knowing when to leave

Aravil defines the Refuge’s initial survival work: wood for fires, fibres for rope and racks for drying hides. In the January hunts her stealth and shooting help companions who are less comfortable in the terrain. She harvests rare components after the first victories, while acknowledging that knowing how to live off a landscape is different from understanding its ecology.

Her confidence has limits. Against an unidentified danger, she reappears with a warning to flee and says they would need stronger support before facing it. Later the group kills a giant serpent, but she botches the harvest. Her own reproach follows a concrete failed task; it does not erase her role in getting the party through the jungle.

    Aravil warns her companions away from an unidentified threat; after a later serpent fight she fails the harvest.

profile.personality: Aravil is concise, observant, and decisive once a fight is truly necessary. She remembers people through the methods and battles they shared, making historical memory one of her clearest forms of respect. Experience appears in judgment and recognition rather than self-promotion.
profile.achievements: She serves as an oathbound hunter, supports Pristinia through hunting, returns when the thrum of war calls, and enters the Abyss with Olokun and Wren. Her critical observation of Zarathian contradictions shows that martial directness does not exhaust her intelligence.
profile.relationships: Her absent Queen remains the origin of her oath. Jiangshi and Scribonia live in her memory through the Fey Forest hunt, including Jiangshi’s violent hairpins; Olokun recognizes her as a returning veteran; and Pristinia becomes a second belonging built through useful work rather than replacement loyalty.
